hints.title: Reverse Accumulation
hints.text: Merging left elements into right elements is easier to evaluate starting from the end of the array.

hints.title: Greedy Merge Step
hints.text: If the element to the left is less than or equal to the current accumulated sum, absorb it into the running sum.

hints.title: Reset When Larger
hints.text: If the element to the left is strictly greater than the accumulated sum, reset the accumulated value to that element.

hints.title: Implementation

complexity.notes: Backward linear scan greedily accumulating smaller or equal adjacent elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating arbitrary pairwise merges from the left creates multiple branching paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) time with a single backward pass and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that a right-to-left scan uniquely maximizes accumulated merge sums.
